f3_program: collection("louise.gathering.cakes", "cake", "gathering", source("cakes for a gathering"))
observe(at("louise.gathering.cakes.required.count", "current"), 60, "count", source("needs 60 cakes in total"))
fraction_of(at("louise.gathering.cakes.produced.count", "already"), at("louise.gathering.cakes.required.count", "current"), 1, 2, source("has already produced half this many"))

difference_relation(at("louise.gathering.cakes.left_to_make.count", "current"), at("louise.gathering.cakes.required.count", "current"), at("louise.gathering.cakes.produced.count", "already"), source("Today, she calculates how many cakes she has left to make"))

remove("louise_bakes_today", "louise", at("louise.gathering.cakes.left_to_make.count", "current"), fraction(at("louise.gathering.cakes.left_to_make.count", "current"), 1, 2), source("bakes half this amount"))

remove("louise_bakes_next_day", "louise", at("louise.gathering.cakes.left_to_make.count", "current"), fraction(at("louise.gathering.cakes.left_to_make.count", "current"), 1, 3), source("bakes a third of this amount"))
query("value", at("louise.gathering.cakes.left_to_make.count", "current"))
assumptions: Each “this amount” refers to the cakes left to make at that point in the narrative.
The source switches from “wooden toys” to “hat,” so it does not specify an unambiguous resale discount for the wooden toys.

f3_program: collection("greg_and_sarah.apples", "apple", "greg_and_sarah", source("Greg and Sarah have 18 apples"))
collection("greg.apples", "apple", "greg", source("Greg and Sarah have 18 apples that they are going to split evenly"))
collection("sarah.apples", "apple", "sarah", source("Greg and Sarah have 18 apples that they are going to split evenly"))
collection("susan.apples", "apple", "susan", source("Susan has twice as many apples as Greg will end up with"))
collection("mark.apples", "apple", "mark", source("Mark has 5 fewer apples than Susan"))

collection("family.apples", "apple", "family", source("Greg and Sarah have 18 apples that they are going to split evenly. Susan has twice as many apples as Greg will end up with. Mark has 5 fewer apples than Susan."))
observe(at("greg_and_sarah.apples.count", "before_split"), 18, "count", source("Greg and Sarah have 18 apples"))

sum_relation(at("greg_and_sarah.apples.count", "before_split"), at("greg.apples.count", "before_pie"), at("sarah.apples.count", "before_pie"), source("Greg and Sarah have 18 apples that they are going to split evenly"))
same(at("greg.apples.count", "before_pie"), at("sarah.apples.count", "before_pie"), source("split evenly"))
multiple(at("susan.apples.count", "before_pie"), at("greg.apples.count", "before_pie"), 2, source("Susan has twice as many apples as Greg will end up with"))
offset(at("mark.apples.count", "before_pie"), at("susan.apples.count", "before_pie"), -5, "count", source("Mark has 5 fewer apples than Susan"))
member("family.apples", "greg.apples", source("Greg and Sarah have 18 apples that they are going to split evenly"))
member("family.apples", "sarah.apples", source("Greg and Sarah have 18 apples that they are going to split evenly"))
member("family.apples", "susan.apples", source("Susan has twice as many apples as Greg will end up with"))
member("family.apples", "mark.apples", source("Mark has 5 fewer apples than Susan"))

partition("family.apples", at("family.apples.count", "before_pie"), source("Greg and Sarah have 18 apples that they are going to split evenly. Susan has twice as many apples as Greg will end up with. Mark has 5 fewer apples than Susan."))
observe(at("mom.apple_pie.apples_required.count", "for_pie"), 40, "count", source("Their mom needs 40 apples to make an apple pie"))
query("difference", at("mom.apple_pie.apples_required.count", "for_pie"), at("family.apples.count", "before_pie"))
assumptions: The apples held by Greg, Sarah, Susan, and Mark form the pool available to their mom before making the pie.
The supplied context neither reports COGS nor states an accounting relation defining it from the displayed metrics.

f3_program: collection("john.dog.vet_appointments", "vet_appointment", "john.dog", source("requires 3 vet appointments"))
collection("john.out_of_pocket_payments", "payment", "john", source("How much did he pay in total?"))
observe(at("john.dog.vet_appointments.count", "total"), 3, "count", source("requires 3 vet appointments"))
observe(at("john.dog.vet_appointments.cost", "per_appointment"), 400, "currency", source("cost $400 each"))
offset(at("john.dog.vet_appointments.subsequent.count", "current"), at("john.dog.vet_appointments.count", "total"), -1, "count", source("After the first appointment"))

product_relation(at("john.dog.vet_appointments.subsequent.cost", "current"), at("john.dog.vet_appointments.subsequent.count", "current"), at("john.dog.vet_appointments.cost", "per_appointment"), source("cost $400 each"))
percent_of(at("john.pet_insurance.covered_cost", "current"), at("john.dog.vet_appointments.subsequent.cost", "current"), 80, source("pet insurance that covers 80% of the subsequent visits"))
same(at("john.out_of_pocket_payments.first_vet_appointment.amount", "current"), at("john.dog.vet_appointments.cost", "per_appointment"), source("cost $400 each"))

difference_relation(at("john.out_of_pocket_payments.subsequent_vet_appointments.amount", "current"), at("john.dog.vet_appointments.subsequent.cost", "current"), at("john.pet_insurance.covered_cost", "current"), source("pet insurance that covers 80% of the subsequent visits"))
observe(at("john.out_of_pocket_payments.pet_insurance_premium.amount", "current"), 100, "currency", source("John paid $100 for pet insurance"))
member("john.out_of_pocket_payments", "john.out_of_pocket_payments.first_vet_appointment.amount", source("cost $400 each"))
member("john.out_of_pocket_payments", "john.out_of_pocket_payments.subsequent_vet_appointments.amount", source("pet insurance that covers 80% of the subsequent visits"))
member("john.out_of_pocket_payments", "john.out_of_pocket_payments.pet_insurance_premium.amount", source("John paid $100 for pet insurance"))
query("sum", "john.out_of_pocket_payments", "current")
assumptions: “Subsequent visits” means the appointments after the first, and John pays the portion of their cost not covered by insurance.
